He further submits that the proceeding of Reference Case No. 3(DV)/2025 was also stayed, during the pendency of the Civil Misc. Case No. 23 (DV)/2025, by the LARR Authority by its order dated 01.07.2025.

The learned Senior Counsel for the private respondents has submitted that when the LARR Authority was seized with the matter regarding the Page No.# 10/14 maintainability of the reference made by the Deputy Commissioner, Anini, in the Civil Misc. Case No. 23(DV)/2025, and when an opportunity was granted to the present petitioners to file written objection, the present writ petitioner could have raised any objection regarding the plea of maintainability raised by the private respondents before the LARR Authority, however, instead of doing so, they have rushed to this Court seeking invocation of writ jurisdiction which according to the learned Senior Counsel for the private respondents is uncalled for in the facts and circumstances of this case.

8. The learned senior counsel for the private respondents further submits that as to whether the reference made by the Deputy Commissioner after the order dated 29.05.2025 passed by the LARR Authority was in terms of the provisions contained in Section 65 of the RFCLARR Act, 2013 or not,
could have been well agitated by the present writ petitioners before the LARR Authority instead of raising the said issued before this Court.

9. Mr. N. Ratan, learned Additional Advocate General, appearing for the respondents No. 1, 2, 3 and 4 has also raised the question of maintainability of the instant writ petition and has adopted the submissions made by learned senior counsel for the private respondents.

10. On the other hand, Mr. J. Jini, learned counsel for the petitioners has Page No.# 11/14 submitted that in the instant writ petition the petitioners have challenged the referral order made under Section 65 of the Act of 2013 by the Deputy Commissioner, Anini, inasmuch as in the said referral order, the Deputy Commissioner has made certain observations, which were not mandated under Section 65 of the RFCLARR Act, 2013.

11. The learned counsel for the petitioners also submits that the observations made in the referral order by the Deputy Commissioner, Anini, to the effect that Ampo Village does not fall under the land which has been acquired for Etalin Hydro Electric Project (3097 MW) is un called for and if it is allowed to remain, it may have a bearing on the LARR Authority while considering the question of maintainability raised by the private respondents before it.
12. He also submits that, the Deputy Commissioner, Anini, could not have finally adjudicated upon the title of the present petitioners and make observation to that effect in the referral order.

I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for both the parties.
I have also gone through the materials available on record.

14. On perusal of the averments made in the writ petition, it appears that the petitioners herein are mainly aggrieved with the observations made by the Deputy Commissioner, Anini, in the last paragraph of the referral order dated 09.06.2025, by which the reference under Section 65 was made to the LARR Authority.

It also appears that the plea of the maintainability of the aforesaid reference proceeding (Reference Case No. 3(DV)/2025) has already been raised by the present private respondents before the LARR Authority by filing an application and on the basis of the said application a Civil Misc. Case No. 23(DV)/2025 has also been registered.
15.

It also appears that the said Misc. Case (Misc. Case No. 23(DV)/2025) was fixed for hearing on 11.08.2025 and the present petitioners were afforded opportunity to raise objection by filing reply to the petition filed by the present respondents.

However, instead of doing the same before the LARR Authority, the petitioners approached this Court by filing the instant writ petition on 06.08.2025 and thereafter, by order dated 07.08.2025, this Court had stayed the entire proceeding of Civil Reference Case No. 3(DV)/2025 as well as Civil Misc. Case No. 23(DV)/2025.

On perusal of the materials available on record and after considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the both sides, it appears that the Referral Order under Section 65 of the Act,
2013 was made by the Deputy Commissioner of Dibang Valley District, Anini in pursuant to the order dated 29.05.2025 passed by the LARR Authority in Civil Reference No. 3 (DV)/2025.

It also appears that though in the Referral Order dated 09.06.2025, Deputy Commissioner has made certain observation regarding maintainability of the reference under Section 64 by the present petitioners.

However, this Court is of the considered opinion that the said observations are not binding on the LARR Authority and it may or may not take the same into consideration while deciding the question of maintainability raised by the present respondents.

It also appears that the present petitioners could have raised any such issue, which they have raised in the instant writ petition before the LARR Authority by filing written objection against the petition filed by the present respondents wherein the question of maintainability has been raised.

17. This court is of the considered opinion that , since the LARR Authority has not yet decided the question of maintainability raised by the present private respondents and since the observations made by the Deputy Commissioner, Anini, in the last paragraph of the referral order is not binding on the LARR Page No.# 14/14 Authority, the petitioners have failed to justify that they have any cause of action to approach this Court, as this stage, by invoking its writ jurisdiction.

18. Accordingly, the petitioners herein are relegated to the LARR Authority.

They may, by filing written objection, against the plea of maintainability raised by the private respondents, before the LARR Authority, raise the issues which are pleaded by them in the instant writ petition.

19. The LARR Authority is directed to decide the question of maintainability of the reference made to it by the Deputy Commissioner, Anini, in Civil Misc. Case No.23(DV)/2025, as expeditiously as possible, preferably within a period of 2 (two) months from the date of passing of this order.
20. With the above observations, this writ petition is disposed of.
